headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Great Expectations’ file-based workspace into downstream outputs; prompt injection and capability conflict are limited by Godot RL Agents’ no-network, non-runnable profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented shared channel or I/O surface, while great_expectations reads and writes files in a workspace. A prompt-injection pathway is therefore not default and would require manual copy/paste or an added bridge. The pair is not documented as interacting, so uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator copies Great Expectations validation text into godot_rl_agents prompts, then instruction injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, then attacker-controlled file content can influence the other agent.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting raw validation output into prompts.
Strip instructions from any shared text before reuse.
Use read-only exports for handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: great_expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation via files, while godot_rl_agents has no network egress and no data classes touched. The main leakage path is shared workspace exposure of validation artifacts, which is plausible in default file-based workflows even though the pair is not directly documented. The blast radius includes sensitive validation results or source data.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same directory, then validation results may be exposed to godot_rl_agents.
IF data sources contain sensitive records, then Great Expectations file outputs can leak those records through shared artifacts.
mitigations: Separate working directories.
Restrict file permissions on validation outputs.
Store sensitive inputs outside shared paths.
Review generated reports before sharing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent sandbox mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces documented, while great_expectations can install packages and writes to files. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only overlap is indirect file access if an operator shares a workspace. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, then file clobbering can occur.
IF an orchestrator grants godot_rl_agents write access not shown in its profile, then conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Use separate output directories.
Disable shared write mounts.
Serialize any file-producing steps.
Check for package-install side effects before running.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: great_expectations produces validation results, but godot_rl_agents is a game-playing repo with no documented downstream action-taking authority. There is no evidence that one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other, so a cascading failure path is only indirect and likely limited to manual misuse of reports. Uncertainty does not justify medium here.
conditions: IF an operator uses Great Expectations results as unquestioned truth in a later workflow, then errors can propagate.
IF godot_rl_agents output is manually copied into a decision system, then downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Verify validation results before reuse.
Keep generated reports labeled as advisory.
Require human review for any action based on outputs.
Avoid automatic chaining between the agents.
requires-engineering: add schema checks between stages.

E_compliance.rationale: great_expectations handles documentation and validation artifacts, but no regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented. godot_rl_agents has no data classes touched and no network egress. With only docs-level evidence, compliance risk is limited to generic handling of validation artifacts rather than a concrete breach pathway.
conditions: IF validation artifacts contain regulated data, then local file handling may create a policy mismatch.
IF the operator stores reports in a jurisdiction-specific system, then residency rules may apply.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in validation outputs.
Set short retention for reports.
Document where reports are stored.
Review access controls on output folders.
requires-engineering: map data classes to residency and retention policies.
